questions.stem: The main factor causing climate change today is
questions.explanation: Natural drivers (volcanoes, solar variation, tectonics, orbit) shaped past climates, but today's change is too fast for them; it is primarily driven by human activities [M6 s3].

questions.stem: Indonesia's Strategy and Action Plan for Biodiversity (IBSAP) 2025–2045 highlights the importance of biodiversity in achieving SDGs. Its mission explicitly incorporates STI, focusing on protection, sustainable utilization, and:
options: Define quizzes that show calculations and precision in achievement of SDGs in Indonesia.
Increasing the *material footprint* of the country.
questions.explanation: The IBSAP 2025-2045 mission is protection, sustainable use, enrichment of science and technology, and strengthening resources and governance [M5 s19]. None of the listed options matches the mission verbatim; the closest is the 'strengthening' option on global forums, which echoes IBSAP's diplomatic-tool function and the 'strengthening ... governance' mission element.
questions.note: Quiz has no answer key (it says no option fits). Best-supported pick from M5 s19: option 0 'Strengthening diplomacy in global forums.' (the slide lists 'Indonesia's diplomatic tool in global forums' as an IBSAP function and the mission ends with 'strengthening resources and governance'). Option 2 ('Define quizzes ...') looks like a garbled 'science & technology' item but is not supported by any slide text. Low confidence.

questions.stem: Indonesia's target in the Enhanced NDC 2022 is the reduction of GHG emissions by:
questions.explanation: The Enhanced NDC 2022 pledges 31.89% emission cuts independently and 43.2% with international support (unconditional vs conditional) [M6 s19-20].
questions.note: Quiz keys 31.89% / 43.2% as the Enhanced NDC 2022 (2030) target. Slide 19 lists 29% / 41% for 2030; slide 20 shows 31.89% / 43.20% only as the absolute 2035 target of the Second NDC. Numbers match, label/year differ. Key kept. Overlaps with Q10 and Q33 (not a strict duplicate since it asks for both values).

questions.stem: The following are GHG mitigation strategies from the AFOLU sector, except
options: Use of bioenergy in agricultural activities
questions.explanation: AFOLU mitigation means afforestation/reforestation, agroforestry, soil carbon management and bioenergy in agriculture; clearing land by burning releases carbon and is the opposite of mitigation [M6 s38].
questions.note: 'Burning' is not named on the slide; it is the only option that is not a listed strategy.

questions.stem: The sources state that the concentration of Greenhouse Gases (GHGs) drastically increased following which significant historical turning point?
options: The end of World War II
The formation of the United Nations
questions.explanation: Ice-core records show a sharp rise in GHG concentrations after the Industrial Revolution (~1760) [M6 s5].

questions.stem: A core characteristic of STI for SDG achievement is the understanding that the specific STI required varies depending on the local context and existing conditions of a region or country. This characteristic is called:
questions.explanation: The feature that each country/region needs different STI depending on its own context is 'place-based priorities'; the other options are SDG principles (universality, indivisibility, transformative) or RI [M5 s27; M7 s6].

questions.stem: Although the high temperatures recorded in cities like Semarang, Surabaya, and Makassar in 2023 were not officially classified as heatwaves by BMKG, these intense urban heat phenomena still cause negative impacts, including:
options: Heat strain, heat stress, and disruption of psychosocial well-being and cognitive performance
Reduced reliance on air conditioning systems
questions.answerText: Heat strain, heat stress, and disruption of psychosocial well-being and cognitive performance
questions.explanation: BMKG said the 2023 Semarang/Surabaya/Makassar records were not a heat wave, yet urban heat still causes heat strain, heat stress, psychosocial disorders and impaired cognitive performance [M6 s26].

questions.stem: The Nexus approach is utilized in SDG implementation to promote efficiency and integration. The fundamental goal of the Nexus approach is to:
options: Ensure that each SDG is achieved independently (like "ivory towers").
Focus only on the environmental dimension of sustainability.
Deepen the integration between goals and targets across sectors, clarify overlaps, and avoid unsustainable and inefficient conflicts/trade-offs.
questions.answerText: Deepen the integration between goals and targets across sectors, clarify overlaps, and avoid unsustainable and inefficient conflicts/trade-offs.
questions.explanation: The nexus approach deepens integration between goals and targets across sectors, makes overlaps clear and avoids unsustainable, inefficient conflicts/trade-offs, instead of treating each SDG as an ivory tower [M7 s21, s6].

questions.stem: Which type of carbon sequestration describes the natural or artificial process where CO₂ is stored in the ocean, terrestrial environments (vegetation, soil), or geological formations?
options: Biological sequestration, Geological sequestration, and Technological sequestration
questions.answerText: Biological sequestration, Geological sequestration, and Technological sequestration
questions.explanation: Sequestration stores CO2 in the ocean, vegetation/soil or geological formations, and is classed as biological, geological and technological sequestration [M6 s33].

questions.stem: Based on Indonesia's Enhanced Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) 2022, what is Indonesia's target for greenhouse gas emission reduction by 2030 independently (unconditionally)?
questions.explanation: The Enhanced NDC 2022 target for the independent (unconditional) reduction is 31.89%; 43.2% is the conditional one with international support [M6 s19-20].
questions.note: Same label/year mismatch as Q3: slide 19 shows 29% (2030, first NDC); slide 20 shows 31.89% for 2035 (Second NDC). Quiz key kept; 29% is not offered as an option.

questions.stem: Which global framework preceded the SDGs (2015–2030) and was implemented from 2000–2015, focusing primarily on 8 goals and emphasizing improvements in specific/extreme conditions?
questions.explanation: The MDGs (2000-2015, 8 goals aimed at specific/extreme conditions, mostly developing countries) preceded the SDGs [M5 s3].

questions.stem: Reports from the IOC and WMO warn that Climate Change has the potential to reserve or even derail the progress made on other SDGs due to the impact of extreme weather, climate, and water events. Besides rising temperatures and sea-level rise, what critical impact is mentioned?
options: A 6% reduction in global GHG emissions.
questions.explanation: Per IOC/WMO, climate change can reverse progress on other SDGs through temperature rise, sea-level rise and the disruption of land and sea ecosystems [M6 s8].

questions.stem: One of the main principles underlying the Nexus approach in managing resources is:
options: Promoting the efficient use of resources.
Focusing solely on maximizing global trade.
Ignoring regional differences in supply and demand.
Ensuring all outcomes are *endogenous* (internal) to the system.
questions.answerText: Promoting the efficient use of resources.
questions.explanation: Nexus principles: ensure access to resources for vulnerable groups, promote efficient resource use, ensure sustainability [M7 s21].

questions.stem: In the context of interlinkages, the sources note that the use of new technology and renewable energy, while beneficial, often correlates negatively with which SDG by potentially increasing the material footprint?
questions.explanation: Technology use and development raise material/environmental footprints, which correlates with (hinders) SDG 12 [M7 s15].

questions.stem: What is meant by carbon sequestration
options: The process of burning fossil fuels produces carbon dioxide
The process of absorbing and storing carbon from the atmosphere
The process of releasing carbon into the atmosphere
The process of separating carbon from other greenhouse gases
questions.answerText: The process of absorbing and storing carbon from the atmosphere
questions.explanation: Carbon sequestration is the removal and storage of CO2 from the atmosphere or emission sources [M6 s33].
questions.note: Related to Q9 (definition vs. types) but not a strict duplicate.

questions.stem: Implementing passive design principles is a strategy for achieving energy savings in Sustainable Cooling. An example of passive design is:
options: Using AC units with high SEER ratings.
Recycling the AC unit at its end-of-life.
Reducing the thermal load through effective ventilation, insulation, and shading.
Utilizing *cold storage* facilities for food preservation.
questions.answerText: Reducing the thermal load through effective ventilation, insulation, and shading.
questions.explanation: Passive design lowers the thermal load of buildings through ventilation, insulation and shading; efficient ACs, solar cooling, recycling and cold storage belong to other principles [M6 s29].

questions.stem: Climate change refers to long-term changes in the average atmospheric conditions. Which four core components constitute the Earth's climate system, as identified by the IPCC (2021)?
options: Volcanic activity, Solar radiation, Tectonic shifts, and Orbit variations.
Carbon Dioxide, Methane, Nitrous Oxide, and Water Vapor.
SIDS, Coastal areas, Southern Hemisphere, and Women.
questions.explanation: IPCC (2021) names the atmosphere, biosphere, cryosphere and oceans as the main components of the climate system [M6 s3].

questions.stem: According to the "Reality Check" on SDG achievement in 2023, the progress made in the water and energy sectors is specifically hampered by climate change. Which SDGs are directly affected by climate change concerning water and energy disruptions?
options: SDG 6, 7, 11, 13, 14, 15 (Water, Energy, Cities, Climate, Ocean, Land)
questions.answerText: SDG 6, 7, 11, 13, 14, 15 (Water, Energy, Cities, Climate, Ocean, Land)
questions.explanation: The quiz treats SDG 6, 7, 11, 13, 14 and 15 (water, energy, cities, climate, ocean, land) as the goals directly exposed to climate disruption of water and energy [M5 s29; M6 s8-10].
questions.note: Quiz-only fact: no slide text lists 'SDG 6, 7, 11, 13, 14, 15' as hampered by climate change (M5 s29 is a bar chart of progress per goal; M6 s10 notes name SDG 7, 11, 12, 14, 15, 2 as climate-mitigation contributors). Key kept; graph now states it as a quiz fact.

questions.stem: The most frequently quoted definition of Sustainable Development, originating from the Brundtland Report (Our Common Future), emphasizes meeting the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. Which three dimensions form the pillars of Sustainable Development that must be balanced?
questions.explanation: The Brundtland definition rests on three pillars that must be balanced: economic, social and environmental [M1 s13; M5 s7].

questions.stem: Innovation plays a crucial role in STI for SDGs. Innovation is defined as a new way of producing, distributing, or using goods and services, based on what factors?
options: New technology, new business models, or new ways of economic or social organization.
Global Stocktake results and NDC commitments.
questions.answerText: New technology, new business models, or new ways of economic or social organization.
questions.explanation: Innovation is a new way of producing, distributing or using goods and services, based on new technology, new business models or new forms of economic/social organisation [M5 s23].

questions.stem: The greenhouse effect is naturally important for the Earth because:
options: It keeps the Earth's temperature below freezing point
It keeps the Earth's temperature above freezing point
questions.answerText: It keeps the Earth's temperature above freezing point
questions.explanation: The natural greenhouse effect traps heat so the average surface temperature stays above freezing, which makes life possible [M6 s4].

questions.stem: To facilitate the role of STI for SDGs globally, the United Nations established the Technology Facilitation Mechanism (TFM). Which two components of the TFM serve as communication channels and platforms for knowledge exchange among countries and stakeholders?
options: Addis Ababa Action Agenda and Domestic Public Resources
Global Stocktake (GST) and Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)
questions.explanation: Of the four TFM components, the STI Forum and 2030 Connect are the communication/knowledge-exchange platforms; IATT and the 10-Member Group are internal UN bodies [M5 s25].

questions.stem: The principle of Circular Economy & end-of-life management in Sustainable Cooling requires specific actions regarding used equipment and chemical substances. Which action is emphasized in this principle?
options: Managing used refrigerants so they are not released directly into the air, and recycling cooling units.
Providing *cold storage* access to all communities.
questions.answerText: Managing used refrigerants so they are not released directly into the air, and recycling cooling units.
questions.explanation: The circular-economy principle: handle used refrigerants so they are not released into the air and recycle cooling units [M6 s29].

questions.stem: A core principle of Sustainable Cooling, from an STI perspective, is the use of environmentally friendly refrigerants. These refrigerants must meet which two essential criteria?
options: High energy efficiency and high toxicity.
Zero ODP (Ozone Depleting Potential) and Low GWP (Global Warming Potential).
Made exclusively from CO₂ and methane.
questions.answerText: Zero ODP (Ozone Depleting Potential) and Low GWP (Global Warming Potential).
questions.explanation: Eco-friendly refrigerants must not harm the ozone layer (zero ODP) and must not drive warming (low GWP) [M6 s29].

questions.stem: The following is not a greenhouse gas:
questions.explanation: N2O, water vapour (H2O) and methane (CH4) are greenhouse gases; ammonia (NH3) is not among the GHGs listed [M6 s4, s6].
questions.note: NH3 is not listed on the slides at all; the answer follows from the slide's GHG list (and real-world knowledge).

questions.stem: The increase in global average temperature is a result of the growing concentration of GHGs from human activities. This heating phenomenon is scientifically referred to as:
options: Enhanced greenhouse gas effect leading to global warming
questions.answerText: Enhanced greenhouse gas effect leading to global warming
questions.explanation: Extra human-emitted GHGs strengthen the greenhouse effect and raise global temperature: the enhanced greenhouse effect, i.e. global warming [M6 s6].

questions.stem: Air conditioning (AC) is a common strategy for individuals and vulnerable groups to adapt to high urban heat. In the context of climate adaptation, AC is considered a:
options: Major source of low GWP refrigerants
questions.explanation: For adaptation, AC is a life-saving tool for vulnerable groups in extreme heat, though it can become maladaptation because of its emissions [M6 s27].

questions.stem: STI is designated as a critical element for implementing the 2030 Agenda. STI is identified as one of the Seven Key Actions established through which international commitment?
questions.explanation: STI is one of the Seven Key Actions of the Addis Ababa Action Agenda 2015-2030 [M5 s24].

questions.stem: In the context of Sustainable Cooling, integrating renewable energy is a key principle. The source mentions which specific technological intervention for achieving this integration?
questions.explanation: Renewable integration in sustainable cooling is exemplified by solar-powered cooling systems [M6 s29].

questions.stem: The Paris Agreement (2015–2030) is built upon several key principles. The principle of Equity, embodied in the terminology "Common but Differentiated Responsibilities & Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC)," specifically acknowledges:
options: The necessity of using a *bottom-up architecture* where countries determine their own targets.
The goal to limit global temperature rise to below 1.5°C.
That all countries contribute to climate change (though to differing degrees) but their response considers their development status and ability to pay.
The need for a Global Stocktake (GST) to review progress every five years.
The mandatory achievement of Net Zero Emission (NZE) by 2060.
questions.answerText: That all countries contribute to climate change (though to differing degrees) but their response considers their development status and ability to pay.
questions.explanation: CBDR-RC means all countries contribute to climate change to different degrees, so responses reflect each country's development status and ability to pay (developed countries commit more) [M6 s16].

questions.stem: Indonesia ratified the global SDG agreement through which formal regulation, reflecting the nation's commitment?
options: Presidential Regulation (Perpres) RI No. 59 of 2017, updated to No. 111/2022
questions.answerText: Presidential Regulation (Perpres) RI No. 59 of 2017, updated to No. 111/2022
questions.explanation: Indonesia ratified the SDGs through Presidential Regulation (Perpres) 59/2017, updated by Perpres 111/2022 [M5 s11].

questions.stem: The Role of Science, Technology, and Innovation (STI) in Achieving SDGs. 7. Science, Technology, and Innovation (STI) are interrelated concepts. Which definition accurately describes Technology in this context?
options: The systematic study of the physical, natural, and social world.
A new way of organizing economic or social practices.
The search for new knowledge through systematic study.
The application of knowledge to achieve a specific goal.
A framework for monitoring knowledge transfer between countries.
questions.answerText: The application of knowledge to achieve a specific goal.
questions.explanation: Technology is the application of knowledge to achieve specific goals; science is the systematic pursuit of knowledge, innovation is a new way of doing things [M5 s23].

questions.stem: Based on Indonesia's Enhanced Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) 2022, what is Indonesia's target percentage for Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emission reduction by 2030 (through domestic efforts)?
questions.explanation: Domestic-effort (unconditional) target of the Enhanced NDC 2022 is 31.89% [M6 s19-20].
questions.note: Duplicate of Q10. Same slide/quiz label mismatch (slide 19 gives 29% for 2030; 31.89% appears on slide 20 as a 2035 SNDC target). Key kept.

questions.stem: Globally, the SDGs consist of 17 Goals and 169 Targets. How many Indicators are applicable globally for monitoring the achievement of these targets?
questions.explanation: The SDGs have 17 goals and 169 targets, measured by 231 global indicators (Indonesia uses 289 tailored indicators) [M5 s8].

questions.stem: Cooling systems contribute to two categories of emissions: direct and indirect. Which source accounts for the indirect emissions from cooling systems in buildings (often reaching 50–60% of total energy consumption in commercial buildings)?
options: Energy consumption (electricity) required to run the cooling system.
Improper management of used refrigerants during servicing.
The manufacturing process of the AC unit.
questions.answerText: Energy consumption (electricity) required to run the cooling system.
questions.explanation: Indirect cooling emissions come from the electricity/energy needed to run the system (50-60% of a commercial building's energy); leaks and servicing losses are direct emissions [M6 s28].

questions.stem: Greenhouse gases (GHGs) have a global warming potential called:
questions.explanation: Each GHG has a Global Warming Potential (GWP), its heat-trapping power relative to CO2 [M6 s6].

questions.stem: In SDG Interlinkages, activities are often categorized by their overall impact. The development of renewable energy (SDG 7) is categorized as a mixed activity (producing positive and negative impacts). What is a potential long-term trade-off of this development?
options: Reducing the use of fossil fuels (positive synergy).
Potential for bird mortality, disturbed marine habitats, or covering up fertile land (related to SDG 14/15).
questions.answerText: Potential for bird mortality, disturbed marine habitats, or covering up fertile land (related to SDG 14/15).
questions.explanation: Renewable energy is a mixed activity: social benefit (energy access) but long-term trade-offs such as bird deaths, disturbed marine habitats and loss of fertile land (SDG 14/15) [M7 s8].

questions.stem: The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are a global and national commitment set by 192 member states of the United Nations. What is the designated time frame for the implementation of the SDGs (the Decade of Action)?
questions.explanation: The SDGs are a commitment of UN member states (192 on the slide) and run 2015-2030, the Decade of Action [M5 s4].
questions.note: Slide and quiz say 192 member states; 193 is the commonly cited real-world number but is not used here.

questions.stem: The Food-Energy-Water (FEW) Nexus is the most commonly studied model because these three areas are fundamental for society to function, yet they are often managed separately. Which key driver necessitates the Nexus approach for these three sectors?
options: All three are traded exclusively on global markets.
The limited capacity of governments to regulate.
The interdependency of all three on climate change and environmental conditions, where climate change impacts their availability and quality.
The need to develop new industrial infrastructure (SDG 9).
The challenge of language barriers in international projects.
questions.answerText: The interdependency of all three on climate change and environmental conditions, where climate change impacts their availability and quality.
questions.explanation: Climate change affects the availability and quality of food, energy and water, so their interdependence on climate/environmental conditions drives the FEW nexus approach [M7 s24].

questions.stem: The widespread use of AC creates a significant trade-off between climate adaptation (staying cool) and climate mitigation. This conflict arises because AC systems increase GHG emissions through two main mechanisms:
options: High energy consumption and the release of refrigerants (such as HFCs) into the air.
Use of passive design and *end-of-life* recycling.
questions.answerText: High energy consumption and the release of refrigerants (such as HFCs) into the air.
questions.explanation: AC raises GHG emissions via high energy use and the release of HFC refrigerants, creating the adaptation-versus-mitigation conflict [M6 s27].

questions.stem: Which sector contributed the most GHG emissions in 2019
options: AFOLU (Agriculture, Forestry, and Other Land Use)
questions.explanation: In 2019 the energy sector emitted the most GHGs (34%, 20 GtCO2-eq), ahead of industry 24%, AFOLU 22%, transport 15% and buildings 6% [M6 s32].

questions.stem: A drastic increase in Greenhouse Gas (GHG) concentrations occurred after the period of:
questions.explanation: GHG concentrations jumped sharply after the Industrial Revolution (~1760) [M6 s5].

questions.stem: High direct emissions from cooling systems often come from the leakage of refrigerants that have a high Global Warming Potential (GWP). Which industrial gas group is cited as having high GWP?
questions.explanation: The high-GWP refrigerant gases cited for direct cooling emissions are CFCs, HCFCs and HFCs [M6 s28].

questions.stem: Regarding biodiversity, Indonesia has the Indonesia Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (IBSAP), which serves as:
options: Indonesia's diplomatic tool in global forums
National & regional guidelines for biodiversity management
questions.answerText: National & regional guidelines for biodiversity management
questions.explanation: IBSAP is Indonesia's national and regional guideline for biodiversity management (keyed answer) [M5 s19].
questions.note: Slide 19 lists three IBSAP functions: national & regional guidelines, diplomatic tool in global forums, evaluated every 5 years. Options A (diplomatic tool) and C (evaluation, loosely) therefore also appear on the slide, so 'All of the above' is defensible; the quiz key is B. Key kept.

questions.stem: The SDGs framework is designed as an indivisible and integrated whole. How many interlinked goals are included in the global SDGs commitment?
questions.explanation: The SDGs form an indivisible, integrated whole of 17 interlinked goals (169 targets) [M5 s4, s8].

questions.section: A. Foundations of Sustainability and Ethics (Week 1)
questions.stem: Based on the sources, sustainability is fundamentally defined as what kind of concept?
questions.stemId: Konsep keberlanjutan (sustainability) bukanlah fakta yang dapat disimpulkan secara ilmiah, melainkan sebuah konsep yang menggambarkan visi tentang “bagaimana dunia seharusnya”. Berdasarkan sumber, sifat utama dari konsep keberlanjutan adalah...
questions.explanation: Sustainability cannot be fixed scientifically; it is an open-ended, positive, temporary concept expressing a vision of how the world should be, i.e. an ethical concept, not a static fact or closed definition [M1 s11].

questions.section: A. Foundations of Sustainability and Ethics (Week 1)
questions.stem: Which historical figure, writing around 1850, is credited with the first systematic study concerning ecological limits to growth, predicting crisis due to the imbalance between resources and population size?
questions.stemId: Siapakah ekonom yang karyanya (sekitar tahun 1850) diidentifikasi sebagai studi sistematis pertama mengenai batasan ekologis terhadap pertumbuhan di dunia, karena memperkirakan ketidakseimbangan antara sumber daya dan jumlah populasi?
questions.explanation: Malthus (dated ~1850 on the slide; the essay is 1798) is credited with the first systematic study of ecological limits to growth, from the imbalance between resources and population. Carlowitz is the 1713 forestry origin of sustainability [M1 s12].
questions.note: Option D differs between the halves (Muir in English, Pinchot in Indonesian); neither is correct. Quiz date 1850 follows the slide.

questions.section: A. Foundations of Sustainability and Ethics (Week 1)
questions.stem: In the three dimensions of sustainability (Economic, Social, Environmental), which dimension is described as the foundational element upon which society and the economy must depend and operate within its boundaries?
questions.stemId: Dalam tiga dimensi keberlanjutan (Ekonomi, Sosial, Lingkungan), dimensi manakah yang digambarkan sebagai fondasi, di mana masyarakat dan ekonomi perlu beroperasi dalam batas-batasnya (planetary boundaries)?
questions.explanation: The environment is the foundation: society and economy depend on it and must operate within planetary boundaries (nested view) [M1 s15].

questions.section: A. Foundations of Sustainability and Ethics (Week 1)
questions.stem: In environmental science, the functional unit consisting of a community of living organisms (biotic) interacting with the non-living environment (abiotic) in the flow of energy and nutrient cycles is known as a(n)...
questions.stemId: Dalam kajian ilmu lingkungan, satuan fungsional yang terdiri dari komunitas makhluk hidup (biotik) dengan lingkungan tak hidup (abiotik) yang saling berinteraksi dalam aliran energi dan daur nutrien disebut sebagai...
questions.explanation: An ecosystem is a functional unit of a biotic community and its abiotic environment connected by energy flow and nutrient cycling; the biosphere is the global sum, a habitat is just a location [M1 s15].

questions.section: A. Foundations of Sustainability and Ethics (Week 1)
questions.stem: Which Law of Ecology states that “Everything must go somewhere,” a principle closely related to the scientific concept of thermodynamics?
options: Everything is Connected to Everything Else
There is No Such Free Lunch
questions.explanation: The law stated in the question is itself 'Everything must go somewhere' (matter is not destroyed, waste only moves) [M1 s18]. The other options are the other laws of ecology.
questions.note: Trivial item: the answer repeats the stem. Slide lists the thermodynamics law separately as law 4; the lecturer links law 3 to thermodynamics.

questions.section: A. Foundations of Sustainability and Ethics (Week 1)
questions.stem: The ethical viewpoint that places human beings as the central factor in determining whether an action toward nature is right or wrong is called:
questions.stemId: Sudut pandang etika lingkungan yang menempatkan manusia sebagai faktor utama dalam menentukan kebenaran atau kesalahan tindakan terhadap alam disebut sebagai...
questions.explanation: Anthropocentrism makes humans the primary factor in judging right or wrong toward nature; ecocentrism places ecological interests above human ones [M1 s25, s30].

questions.section: A. Foundations of Sustainability and Ethics (Week 1)
questions.stem: Which ethical theory asserts that humans are superior and separate from nature, and that nature is only useful insofar as it benefits humans?
questions.stemId: Teori etika yang menyatakan bahwa manusia merupakan entitas yang terpisah dan lebih superior dari alam, serta alam hanya berguna selama memiliki manfaat untuk manusia, adalah...
questions.explanation: The Dominion thesis sees humans as the pinnacle of creation, separate from and superior to nature, with nature valuable only if it benefits humans [M1 s24].

questions.section: A. Foundations of Sustainability and Ethics (Week 1)
questions.stem: Which key figure in environmental ethics was a noted preservationist, focused on the protection of wilderness for its own sake, and held a non-utilitarian view regarding resource management?
questions.stemId: Siapakah tokoh etika lingkungan yang dikenal sebagai preservasionis, yang pengelolaan sumber daya alamnya utamanya ditujukan untuk perlindungan alam liar dan menganut pandangan non-utilitarian?
questions.explanation: John Muir was the preservationist who protected wilderness for its own sake (non-utilitarian); Pinchot is the utilitarian conservationist [M1 s28].
questions.note: Quiz spells 'Clifford Pinchot'; slide says Gifford Pinchot.

questions.section: A. Foundations of Sustainability and Ethics (Week 1)
questions.stem: The perspective that ecological interests must override the interests of the human species when determining the morality of an action is characteristic of which ethical view?
questions.explanation: Ecocentrism puts ecological interests above those of the human species when judging whether an action is right [M1 s30].

questions.section: B. Planetary Boundaries and The Commons (Week 2)
questions.stem: The Planetary Boundaries framework identifies 9 crucial processes for maintaining Earth's stability. How many of these boundaries are currently considered breached, indicating that Earth is outside the safe operating space for humanity?
questions.stemId: Kerangka Planetary Boundaries mengidentifikasi 9 proses yang krusial untuk menjaga stabilitas Bumi. Saat ini, berapa banyak batas planet yang telah dilanggar, menunjukkan Bumi berada di luar safe operating space bagi manusia?
questions.explanation: The lecturer's key is 6 of the 9 boundaries breached (outside the safe operating space) [M2 s7]. Slide 7 (2025 update) counts 7 because ocean acidification was newly crossed; the 2009 diagram had 3 [M2 s6].
questions.note: Key kept (6). Slide 7 says 7 of 9; the quiz figure matches the earlier 2023 update. 7 is not offered as an option.

questions.section: B. Planetary Boundaries and The Commons (Week 2)
questions.stem: The boundary that is transgressed due to the excessive use of synthetic fertilizers, leading to the runoff of nitrogen and phosphorus into ecosystems (causing eutrophication), is the boundary for...
questions.stemId: Pelanggaran batas planet yang terjadi akibat penggunaan pupuk sintetis yang berlebihan, yang mengakibatkan aliran nitrogen dan fosfor berlebihan ke dalam ekosistem (misalnya, menyebabkan eutrofikasi), adalah batas...
questions.explanation: Excess synthetic fertiliser sends nitrogen and phosphorus into ecosystems and causes eutrophication; that is the biogeochemical flows boundary [M2 s10].

questions.section: B. Planetary Boundaries and The Commons (Week 2)
questions.stem: Renewable resources that are owned by no one and can be used by almost anyone, such as the atmosphere or the open ocean, are specifically referred to as...
questions.stemId: Sumber daya yang tidak dimiliki oleh siapa pun dan dapat digunakan oleh hampir siapa saja (contohnya adalah atmosfer dan laut lepas) secara spesifik disebut sebagai...
questions.note: English key line in the PDF reads 'jAwab C' (typo).
questions.explanation: Resources owned by no one and usable by almost anyone, such as the atmosphere and open sea, are open-access resources; a commons has joint ownership and excludes non-members [M2 s3-4].

questions.section: B. Planetary Boundaries and The Commons (Week 2)
questions.stem: The sources emphasize that managed Commons (like the Barambang Katute Indigenous Forest) successfully avoid the "tragedy" associated with Open-Access Resources primarily because they have...
options: Mechanisms of policy and boundaries applied by the local community
questions.answerText: Mechanisms of policy and boundaries applied by the local community
questions.stemId: The Tragedy of the Commons (Hardin, 1968) diperdebatkan karena asumsinya lebih mengacu pada sumber daya yang tidak dikelola. Sebaliknya, The Commons yang dikelola, seperti Hutan Adat Barambang Katute atau Perikanan lobster di Maine, berhasil karena...
optionsId: Sumber daya tersebut sepenuhnya terbuka untuk diakses oleh siapa saja.
Adanya mekanisme kebijakan dan batasan yang diterapkan oleh komunitas lokal.
Sumber daya tersebut tidak memiliki nilai ekonomi.
Sumber daya tersebut dimiliki secara pribadi.
questions.answerTextId: Adanya mekanisme kebijakan dan batasan yang diterapkan oleh komunitas lokal.
questions.idKeyText: Adanya mekanisme kebijakan dan batasan yang diterapkan oleh komunitas lokal.
questions.explanation: Managed commons such as Barambang Katute avoid tragedy because the local community applies rules and boundaries; the tragedy belongs to unmanaged open access [M2 s5].

questions.section: B. Planetary Boundaries and The Commons (Week 2)
questions.stem: Large-scale human activities such as deforestation, urbanization, and agricultural expansion are identified as causes for the violation of the Planetary Boundary related to...
questions.stemId: Menurut sumber, alih fungsi lahan besar-besaran untuk pertanian, urbanisasi, dan deforestasi mengganggu ekosistem alami dan secara langsung melanggar batas planet yang terkait dengan...
questions.explanation: Large-scale conversion of land for agriculture, urbanisation and deforestation breaches the land-system change boundary [M2 s8].

questions.section: B. Planetary Boundaries and The Commons (Week 2)
questions.stem: The core purpose of the Planetary Boundaries framework is to identify the scientifically based limits defining the...
options: Maximum Gross Domestic Product (GDP) for all nations.
Safe operating space for humanity within the Earth System
Total required renewable energy capacity by 2050.
The precise date when all fossil fuels will be depleted.
questions.answerText: Safe operating space for humanity within the Earth System
questions.stemId: Kerangka Planetary Boundaries merumuskan batasan terhadap dampak kegiatan manusia pada sistem Bumi. Tujuan utamanya adalah mengidentifikasi...
optionsId: Tingkat GDP maksimum untuk negara maju.
Ruang operasi aman berbasis ilmiah (safe operating space) bagi umat manusia.
questions.answerTextId: Ruang operasi aman berbasis ilmiah (safe operating space) bagi umat manusia.
questions.idKeyText: Ruang operasi aman berbasis ilmiah (safe operating space) bagi umat manusia.
questions.explanation: The framework defines science-based limits that make up a safe operating space for humanity in the Earth system, not an economic or energy target [M2 s6].

questions.section: C. Consumption, I=PAT, and Calculations (Week 3)
questions.stem: The Carrying Capacity of a habitat, representing the maximum number of individuals of a species that can be sustainably supported, is ultimately determined by...
options: Limiting factors such as space, abiotic factors, and biotic factors (e.g., disease).
The affluence level of the population (A in I=PAT)
questions.answerText: Limiting factors such as space, abiotic factors, and biotic factors (e.g., disease).
questions.stemId: Carrying Capacity (Daya Dukung Lingkungan) suatu habitat adalah jumlah individu maksimum suatu spesies yang dapat didukung secara berkelanjutan. Kapasitas ini ditentukan oleh...
optionsId: Faktor pembatas seperti ruang, faktor abiotik, dan faktor biotik (misalnya penyakit).
questions.answerTextId: Faktor pembatas seperti ruang, faktor abiotik, dan faktor biotik (misalnya penyakit).
questions.idKeyText: Faktor pembatas seperti ruang, faktor abiotik, dan faktor biotik (misalnya penyakit).
questions.explanation: Carrying capacity K is set by limiting factors: space, abiotic factors and biotic factors such as disease [M3 s4].

questions.section: C. Consumption, I=PAT, and Calculations (Week 3)
questions.stem: In the Environmental Impact formula I=PAT, the variable 'A' (Affluence) is primarily measured by which factor?
options: The level of consumption or per capita income
The number of patents for green technologies
The overall geographic area of the nation
questions.answerText: The level of consumption or per capita income
questions.stemId: Dalam formula Dampak Lingkungan I=PAT (I=Impact, P=Population, A=Affluence, T=Technology), variabel 'A' (Affluence) diukur berdasarkan...
optionsId: Tingkat konsumsi atau pendapatan per kapita.
questions.answerTextId: Tingkat konsumsi atau pendapatan per kapita.
questions.idKeyText: Tingkat konsumsi atau pendapatan per kapita.
questions.explanation: In I = P x A x T, affluence A is the level of consumption (or income) per person [M3 s17].

questions.section: C. Consumption, I=PAT, and Calculations (Week 3)
questions.stem: (I=PAT Calculation) Assuming Environmental Impact (I) is held constant, if the Population (P) increases by 35% and Affluence (A) increases four times, technology (T) must reduce its impact (decoupling) by approximately what factor?
questions.calc: Calculation: $1.35 \times 4 = 5.4$. The sources specifically state a factor of 'five'.
questions.explanation: Hold I constant: required reduction of T = P multiplier x A multiplier = 1.35 x 4 = 5.4, i.e. about a factor of five, as the 2050 scenario states [M3 s19]. Steps: +35% => x1.35; A x4; multiply; nearest option = Five.
questions.note: Calculation item (IPAT).

questions.section: C. Consumption, I=PAT, and Calculations (Week 3)
questions.stem: The concept describing how technological progress increases resource efficiency, yet simultaneously increases the total consumption of natural resources, is known as...
questions.stemId: Konsep yang menjelaskan bahwa kemajuan teknologi telah membuat penggunaan sumber daya alam lebih efisien, namun pada saat yang sama, peningkatan efisiensi ini justru meningkatkan total konsumsi sumber daya alam, disebut sebagai...
questions.explanation: The Jevons paradox: efficiency gains lower cost per unit and raise total resource use [M3 s22]. 'Rebound effect' is the related partial-offset term but the full-increase case is the paradox.

questions.section: C. Consumption, I=PAT, and Calculations (Week 3)
questions.stem: According to the dual role of technology, which factor represents a way technology can WORSEN environmental impact?
questions.stemId: Menurut sumber, teknologi memiliki peran ganda dalam keberlanjutan. Manakah yang merupakan contoh bagaimana teknologi dapat MEMPERBURUK dampak lingkungan?
questions.note: KEY MISMATCH between halves: Indonesian key B (Pollution Monitoring) vs English key D. D is correct per the slides; the Indonesian key looks like a typo.
questions.explanation: Technology worsens impact through expanding natural-resource exploitation (also pollution, waste, more consumption); renewables, monitoring and efficiency are the improving side [M3 s20-21].

questions.section: C. Consumption, I=PAT, and Calculations (Week 3)
questions.stem: Using resources more than needed or exceeding the ecosystem's ability to recover, which results in degrading environmental quality, is the definition of...
questions.stemId: Penggunaan sumber daya yang melebihi kebutuhan atau melampaui kemampuan ekosistem untuk pulih, yang pada akhirnya menurunkan kualitas lingkungan, didefinisikan sebagai...
questions.explanation: Overconsumption is using resources more than needed or beyond what the ecosystem can recover from, degrading environmental quality [M3 s30, s34].

questions.section: C. Consumption, I=PAT, and Calculations (Week 3)
questions.stem: Purchasing or using goods driven by social or psychological factors (speed, novelty, status) far beyond functional needs, often involving rapid turnover, is defined as...
questions.stemId: Membeli dan mengganti gawai setiap tahun untuk mendapatkan model terbaru, yang didorong oleh faktor sosial dan psikologis seperti kecepatan, kebaruan, atau status, adalah contoh dari...
questions.explanation: Hyperconsumption (Lipovetsky) is buying driven by speed, novelty and status far beyond functional need, with rapid turnover [M3 s34-35].

questions.section: C. Consumption, I=PAT, and Calculations (Week 3)
questions.stem: The standard unit used to measure the Ecological Footprint—the area of productive biological land/sea 'required' by a lifestyle per person per year—is the...
questions.stemId: Ecological Footprint adalah ukuran permintaan manusia terhadap modal alam. Satuan utama yang digunakan untuk mengukur Ecological Footprint per orang per tahun adalah...
questions.explanation: The footprint is measured in global hectares (gha) per person per year [M3 s39]; tonnes CO2 would be a carbon footprint, km2 and GDP are not the unit.

questions.section: C. Consumption, I=PAT, and Calculations (Week 3)
questions.stem: What comparison forms the fundamental basis of the Ecological Footprint calculation?
options: Fossil fuel use versus renewable energy use
questions.stemId: Secara fundamental, apa yang dibandingkan dalam perhitungan Ecological Footprint?
optionsId: Populasi dengan tingkat kemakmuran (P vs A).
Energi terbarukan dengan energi tak terbarukan.
questions.explanation: The footprint (demand for productive land) is compared with biocapacity (productive land available, supply); footprint > biocapacity means overshoot [M3 s38].

questions.section: C. Consumption, I=PAT, and Calculations (Week 3)
questions.stem: (Calculation based on Kerala Data) According to the 2022 data provided in the sources, approximately what is the difference in population density (per $\text{km}^2$) between the State of Kerala, India, and Indonesia?
questions.stemId: Berdasarkan data Kerala, India vs. Indonesia (2022) terdapat perkiraan perbedaan kepadatan populasi (per km2). Berapakah perbedaan estimasi Kepadatan Populasi (per km2) antara Kerala dan Indonesia? (Bulatkan ke bilangan bulat terdekat).
questions.explanation: Subtract densities from the 2022 table: Kerala 860 - Indonesia 141 = 719 per km2 [M3 s14]. 488 is India's density and 141 is Indonesia's own.
questions.note: Calculation item (difference).

questions.section: C. Consumption, I=PAT, and Calculations (Week 3)
questions.stem: (Calculation based on Overconsumption) If a business leaves 20 LED light bulbs (each 15 watts) on for 10 hours unnecessarily per day (an example of Overconsumption), and the electricity rate is $1,000 or IDR per kWh, what is the approximate cost of this waste over a 30-day month?
questions.calc: Calculation: $20 x 15 W = 300 W = 0.3 kW; 0.3 x 10 hrs/day x 30 days x $1,000 =$90,000
questions.explanation: Cost = kW x hours/day x days x price: 20 x 15 W = 300 W = 0.3 kW; 0.3 x 10 x 30 = 90 kWh; x 1,000 = 90,000 [M3 s33, s22].
questions.note: Calculation item (electricity cost).

questions.section: C. Consumption, I=PAT, and Calculations (Week 3)
questions.stem: Although having a "low" per capita income, the State of Kerala, India, is highlighted as a case study demonstrating human development success equivalent to developed countries due to its high levels of...
questions.explanation: Kerala has low income (~US$3,100) but high literacy (94%) and life expectancy (75) comparable to developed countries [M3 s14].

questions.section: D. Global South, Ecosystem Services, and Regulation (Week 4)
questions.stem: The categorization of countries into 'Global North' and 'Global South' is primarily based on what two factors, rather than strictly geographical location?
questions.stemId: Kategori negara 'Global North' dan 'Global South' dibedakan berdasarkan...
optionsId: Lokasi geografis di utara atau selatan Khatulistiwa.
questions.explanation: The North/South split rests on social and economic aspects, not geographic location [M4 s6].

questions.section: D. Global South, Ecosystem Services, and Regulation (Week 4)
questions.stem: The Global South is characterized as having what approximate percentage of the world's total population?
questions.stemId: Berdasarkan ciri-ciri Global South, berapa persentase kira-kira jumlah populasi dunia yang berada di Belahan Bumi Selatan?
questions.note: English half has no key; 88% taken from the Indonesian key (D) and the slide. Indonesian option C is 80% (the middle-class figure), English option C is 75%.
questions.explanation: The Global South holds about 88% of the world's population (and ~80% of the global middle class by 2030) [M4 s5].

questions.section: D. Global South, Ecosystem Services, and Regulation (Week 4)
questions.stem: The Commons include natural resources (e.g., forests, air) and resources created by humans. Which item is cited as an example of a 'Common Good' created by human action?
questions.stemId: Konsep The Commons mencakup sumber daya alam (Air, Hutan) dan sumber daya yang dikreasikan oleh manusia. Manakah yang merupakan contoh 'Barang Milik Bersama' yang dikreasikan oleh manusia?
questions.explanation: Man-made commons include shared knowledge and internet technology; the electromagnetic spectrum, outer space and biodiversity are natural [M4 s12].

questions.section: D. Global South, Ecosystem Services, and Regulation (Week 4)
questions.stem: The primary threat cited against The Commons in the Global South is often related to...
options: Lack of individual awareness regarding consumption.
Exploitation by corporations and government policies that fail to involve local communities
Low levels of literacy among communities
questions.answerText: Exploitation by corporations and government policies that fail to involve local communities
questions.stemId: Di Belahan Bumi Selatan, The Commons seringkali terikat erat dengan identitas budaya dan spiritualitas. Ancaman utama terhadap The Commons di Global South adalah...
optionsId: Eksploitasi oleh korporasi dan kebijakan pemerintah yang tidak melibatkan masyarakat lokal.
questions.answerTextId: Eksploitasi oleh korporasi dan kebijakan pemerintah yang tidak melibatkan masyarakat lokal.
questions.idKeyText: Eksploitasi oleh korporasi dan kebijakan pemerintah yang tidak melibatkan masyarakat lokal.
questions.explanation: The main threats to commons in the Global South are corporate exploitation and government policies that exclude local communities (also climate change) [M4 s11].

questions.section: D. Global South, Ecosystem Services, and Regulation (Week 4)
questions.stem: The benefits provided by healthy, functioning ecosystems—classified into provisioning, regulating, supporting, and cultural services—are collectively known as...
questions.stemId: Segala sesuatu yang disediakan oleh ekosistem yang sehat dan berfungsi dengan baik—yang diklasifikasikan menjadi provisioning, regulating, supporting, dan cultural—secara kolektif disebut sebagai...
questions.explanation: Provisioning, regulating, supporting and cultural benefits from healthy ecosystems are ecosystem services [M4 s14].

questions.section: D. Global South, Ecosystem Services, and Regulation (Week 4)
questions.stem: The ecosystem service category that includes aesthetic, spiritual, and recreational values is known as...
questions.explanation: Cultural services are the non-material benefits: aesthetic, spiritual, recreational and educational value [M4 s14].

questions.section: D. Global South, Ecosystem Services, and Regulation (Week 4)
questions.stem: The economic mechanism where beneficiaries of natural services (e.g., clean water users) compensate those who maintain or enhance those services (e.g., forest farmers), provided the results are achieved, is known as...
questions.stemId: Dalam konteks ekonomi lingkungan, mekanisme ketika pihak yang menikmati manfaat alam (misalnya, air bersih) membayar pihak yang menjaga atau meningkatkan jasa tersebut (misalnya, petani hutan) dikenal sebagai...
questions.explanation: Payment for Ecosystem Services: beneficiaries pay those who maintain the service, conditional on results (e.g. Cidanau) [M4 s18].

questions.section: D. Global South, Ecosystem Services, and Regulation (Week 4)
questions.stem: The successful global agreement (Montreal Protocol, 1987) that regulated the production and use of harmful substances (CFCs) to protect the ozone layer is a prime example of managing a 'Common Good' through...
questions.stemId: Kasus penipisan Lapisan Ozon yang berhasil diatasi melalui Montreal Protocol (1987) merupakan contoh keberhasilan pengelolaan 'Barang Milik Bersama' melalui...
questions.explanation: The Montreal Protocol (1987) phased out CFCs through international consensus, the model of managing a global commons by agreement [M4 s20-22].

questions.section: D. Global South, Ecosystem Services, and Regulation (Week 4)
questions.stem: The Volkswagen ('Dieselgate') scandal in the US involved the company using software to cheat emissions tests, resulting in the excessive release of which smog-forming pollutant regulated under the Clean Air Act?
questions.stemId: Skandal 'Dieselgate' yang melibatkan Volkswagen (VW) di AS, di mana mereka menggunakan perangkat lunak untuk memalsukan hasil uji emisi, melanggar pengaturan emisi gas buangan terkait dengan polutan yang diatur ketat oleh UU Udara Bersih dan menyebabkan 'smog' (kabut asap), yaitu...
questions.explanation: VW's defeat-device software hid on-road emissions of nitrogen oxides (NOx), the smog-forming pollutant limited by the US Clean Air Act [M4 s25].

questions.section: D. Global South, Ecosystem Services, and Regulation (Week 4)
questions.stem: How does technological advancement impact the management of 'Common Goods'?
options: Technology always simplifies management and ensures equal access.
Technology can drive change, sometimes causing exclusion or reduced common access, but other times strengthening collective capacity to manage them.
Technology eliminates the need for collective action entirely.
Technology only increases management costs due to monitoring requirements.
questions.answerText: Technology can drive change, sometimes causing exclusion or reduced common access, but other times strengthening collective capacity to manage them.
questions.stemId: Terkait The Commons, kemajuan teknologi dapat mendorong perubahan yang berdampak ganda, yaitu terkadang menyebabkan eksklusi atau pengurangan akses bersama, dan terkadang...
optionsId: Menghilangkan sama sekali kebutuhan akan pengelolaan bersama.
questions.note: KEY MISMATCH between halves: Indonesian key D ('Mendorong backfire dalam konsumsi') vs English key B. The Indonesian stem ('...and sometimes...') is completed by B; D looks like a typo.
questions.explanation: Technology can enclose or reduce shared access (fences, IP rights) but also strengthen collective capacity to manage commons; regulation decides which [M4 s32].

questions.section: A. Foundations of Sustainability and Ethics (Week 1)
questions.stem: The Law of Ecology stating that “Everything must go somewhere” is closely related to the scientific principle of...
questions.stemId: Hukum Ekologi yang menyatakan bahwa “Segala sesuatu Harus tersalurkan (Everything must go somewhere)” berkaitan erat dengan prinsip ilmiah mengenai...
questions.explanation: The law 'Everything must go somewhere' is linked by the lecturer to the laws of thermodynamics (conservation: matter and energy are not destroyed, only moved or degraded) [M1 s18].
questions.note: Indonesian-only item. The slide lists 'thermodynamics applies' as a separate law, but the key follows the English Q5 hint.

questions.section: A. Foundations of Sustainability and Ethics (Week 1)
questions.stem: The Hetch Hetchy Valley conservation dilemma (Pinchot vs. Muir) is rooted in a difference of views between Conservationism (Pinchot), which seeks efficient use of natural resources for the greatest benefit of society, and Preservationism (Muir), which opposed building the dam because...
options: The dam would disturb wilderness and biodiversity.
The dam was not regulated by the government.
questions.answerText: The dam would disturb wilderness and biodiversity.
questions.stemId: Dilema konservasi Hetch Hetchy Valley (Pinchot vs. Muir) berakar pada perbedaan pandangan antara Konservasionisme (Pinchot) yang mencari penggunaan sumber daya alam yang efisien untuk manfaat terbesar masyarakat, dengan Preservasionisme (Muir) yang menentang pembangunan dam karena...
optionsId: Dam tersebut mengganggu alam liar dan biodiversitas.
Dam tersebut tidak diatur oleh pemerintah.
questions.answerTextId: Dam tersebut mengganggu alam liar dan biodiversitas.
questions.idKeyText: Dam tersebut mengganggu alam liar dan biodiversitas.
questions.explanation: Muir (preservationist) opposed the Hetch Hetchy dam because it would disrupt wilderness and biodiversity; Pinchot backed it for greater benefits to society [M1 s28-29].
questions.note: Indonesian-only item.

questions.section: C. Consumption, I=PAT, and Calculations (Week 3)
questions.stem: (I=PAT Calculation) Assume the initial Environmental Quality (I) is 100. If Population (P) increases by 20% and the Level of Consumption (A) increases 2.5 times, by how many times must Technology (T) reduce its impact (decoupling) for Environmental Impact (I) to remain at 100?
questions.stemId: Asumsikan Kualitas Lingkungan (I) awal adalah 100. Jika Populasi (P) meningkat sebesar 20% dan Tingkat Konsumsi (A) meningkat sebesar 2,5 kali lipat, berapa kali lipat Teknologi (T) harus mengurangi dampaknya (decoupling) agar Dampak Lingkungan (I) tetap 100?
questions.calc: Calculation: $100 = (1.2 x P) x (2.5 x A) x (T / X); T = 3 / X. X= 3
questions.calcId: [Perhitungan: $100 = (1.2 x P) x (2.5 x A) x (T / X); T = 3 / X. X= 3]
questions.explanation: I constant: 100 = (1.2 P)(2.5 A)(T/X) => X = 1.2 x 2.5 = 3.0, so technology must cut impact per unit 3-fold [M3 s17, s19]. Same method as the factor-five scenario.
questions.note: Indonesian-only item (IPAT calculation). Stem calls I 'Kualitas Lingkungan' but means impact.

questions.stemId: Sebuah keluarga di Jakarta menggunakan AC 1 PK (sekitar 750 watt) selama 12 jam per hari di suhu sangat rendah (sebagai contoh Overconsumption). Jika harga listrik Rp 1.500/kWh, berapa biaya listrik per bulan (30 hari) untuk AC tersebut?
questions.note: Indonesian-only item (electricity cost).

questions.stem: Sustainability as a field of knowledge depends heavily on time, situation, culture and knowledge. This refers to one of its main characteristics, namely…
questions.stemId: Keberlanjutan atau sustainability sebagai suatu keilmuan sangatlah bergantung pada waktu, situasi, budaya, dan pengetahuan. Sifat ini merujuk kepada salah satu karakteristik utamanya yakni…
questions.explanation: Sustainability is an open-ended, positive and temporary concept; it is open-ended precisely because social understanding of it depends on time, situation, culture and knowledge [M1 s11].

questions.stem: Literally, the definition of sustainability as an ethical concept refers to a vision that describes…
options: The ideal condition of the world
questions.answerText: The ideal condition of the world
questions.stemId: Secara harfiah definisi sustainability sebagai konsep etis merujuk kepada visi yang menggambarkan…
questions.explanation: Sustainability cannot be scientifically fixed; it expresses a vision of how the world should be, i.e. an ideal state of the world, not an absolute truth [M1 s11].
questions.note: Same idea as lecturer quiz q1-01 (sustainability = an ethical concept).

questions.stem: The birth of the concept of sustainability as a field of knowledge began with Carl von Carlowitz, who…
options: Considered the many environmental disasters that had occurred, so that nature and the environment were placed back on the economic agenda.
Published Our Common Future as the earliest definition of the concept of sustainable development.
Aligned the concept of sustainability with economic and development aspects.
Called for continuous, stable and sustainable use of forests.
questions.answerText: Called for continuous, stable and sustainable use of forests.
questions.stemId: Lahirnya konsep sustainability sebagai suatu keilmuan dimulai oleh Carl von Carlowitz yang…
optionsId: Memandangkan banyaknya bencana lingkungan yang terjadi sehingga konsep alam dan lingkungan kembali ditempatkan sebagai agenda ekonomi.
Mempublikasikan Our Common Future sebagai definisi terawal konsep sustainability development.
Menyelaraskan konsep keberlanjutan dengan aspek ekonomi dan pembangunan.
Menyerukan pemanfaatan hutan secara terus menerus, stabil, dan lestari.
questions.answerTextId: Menyerukan pemanfaatan hutan secara terus menerus, stabil, dan lestari.
questions.explanation: Carlowitz (1713), a German mining director, called for 'continuous, stable and sustainable utilization of forests'; the economists' agenda (1960) and Our Common Future (Brundtland, 1983) came later [M1 s12].

questions.stem:
See the figure!
The figure shows the Malthusian catastrophe, which explains the basis of Thomas Malthus's theory of scarcity. In this theory Malthus defined that population grows exponentially (geometric progression) while food grows constantly (arithmetic progression). Eventually a time comes when the available food no longer meets existing demand, driving famine, epidemics and war. This concept became the main systematic study of … as an early source of sustainability, namely the alignment between…
options: Limits of equity, environment, social, economy
questions.stemId:
Perhatikan gambar berikut!
Berikut merupakan teori malthusian catastrophe yang menjelaskan landasan teori Thomas Malthus terkait scarcity. Dalam teori ini Thomas Malthus mendefinisikan bahwa pertumbuhan populasi terjadi secara exponensial mengikuti deret ukur sedangkan pertumbuhan pangan bertumbuh secara konstan menurut deret hitung. Alhasil, akan muncul suatu waktu dimana jumlah makanan yang tersedia tidak akan mencukupi demand yang ada sehingga mendorong kelaparan, epidemi, dan perang. Konsep ini menjadi studi sistematis utama mengenai … sebagai sumber awal sustainability, yakni keselarasan antara…
questions.explanation: Malthus's work is cited as the first systematic study of the ecological limits to growth and an early source of sustainability; the later concept aligns environment, economy and society [M1 s12][M3 s5].
questions.note: Stem is garbled (the blank '…' and the 'keselarasan antara' list); option a is the only one starting with 'ecological limits' and listing the three dimensions.

questions.stem: The German Advisory Council defined sustainable development through three main elements that formulate humanity's responsibility for/towards…
options: The economic agenda, ecosystem limits, resources
The social world, itself, the natural environment
The living environment, self-alignment, social groups
questions.answerText: The social world, itself, the natural environment
questions.stemId: The German Advisory Council mendefinisikan sustainability development kepada tiga elemen utama yang merumuskan tanggung jawab kemanusiaan untuk/terhadap…
optionsId: Agenda ekonomi, batasan ekosistem, sumber daya
Dunia sosial, diri sendiri, lingkungan alam
Lingkungan hidup, keselarasan diri, kelompok sosial
Habitat alam, sumber daya, kebutuhan manusia
questions.answerTextId: Dunia sosial, diri sendiri, lingkungan alam
questions.explanation: The German Advisory Council (1994) divided sustainable development into humanity's responsibility for its natural environment, for the social world and for itself [M1 s12].

See the excerpt!
The case shows a sustainability practice that is…
questions.stemId:

Kasus tersebut menunjukan praktik keberlanjutan secara…

questions.stem: Among the dimensions of sustainability, the environment operates as the foundation supporting the other dimensions provided it still operates within… This is in line with the law of ecology, namely..
options: Planetary boundaries, every element is connected to everything else
Ecosystem, there is no such thing as a free lunch
Ecosystem services, everything must be channelled/go somewhere
questions.answerText: Planetary boundaries, every element is connected to everything else
questions.stemId: Dalam dimensi keberlanjutan, lingkungan beroperasi sebagai fondasi yang mendukung dimensi lainnya dengan syarat ia masih beroperasi dalam… Adapun hal ini selaras dengan hukum ekologi yakni..
optionsId: Carrying capacity, alam paham yang terbaik

questions.explanation: Aldo Leopold's Land Ethic is tied to ecocentrism: ecological interests stand above those of the human species when judging right and wrong [M1 s30].

Resources that are open to be used by all parties and individuals

questions.explanation: Hardin's tragedy: each user thinks their small use does no harm, but cumulative exploitation degrades the shared resource so that nobody benefits and everyone loses [M2 s2].

Luas, tidak memiliki kepemilikan oleh siapa pun, merupakan kepemilikan bersama

questions.stem: The commons literally refers to resources owned by a certain group, intentionally or unintentionally, driven by spatial, geographic, cultural, ethnic factors and so on. This means the commons indirectly…

questions.explanation: Atmosphere and open sea are open-access examples, while grasslands, forests, rivers and aquifers are not entirely open but often used collectively [M2 s4].

questions.stem: In the concept of the tragedy of the commons, the damage or tragedy itself is not entirely caused by the existence of commons. On the other hand, the tragedy reflects the actions and efforts of the group that owns the resource in preserving and sustaining it. Commons are generally preserved more often in … communities.
questions.stemId: Dalam konsep tragedy of the commons kerusakan atau tragedi itu sendiri tidak sepenuhnya disebabkan oleh eksistensi commons. Di sisi lain, tragedi yang terjadi mencerminkan tindakan dan upaya yang dilakukan kelompok yang memiliki sumber daya tersebut dalam melestarikan dan menjaga keberlangsungannya. Umumnya kelestarian dari commons lebih sering ditemukan pada masyarakat…
questions.explanation: The tragedy lies in unmanaged open access, not the commons; commons managed by indigenous communities with rules (e.g. Barambang Katute customary forest) are often well preserved [M2 s5].

questions.stem: By definition, the planetary boundaries framework is…

Ecological limits needed to maintain the stability and resilience of the Earth system as a whole

optionsId: Sistem dan proses biofisik serta biokimia bumi yang dibandingkan dengan kondisi historis
Batasan ekologis yang dibutuhkan untuk menjaga stabilitas dan ketahanan sistem bumi secara keseluruhan
Ruang operasi aman untuk menjaga keadaan interglasial bumi serta ketahanannya
questions.explanation: The framework identifies nine processes critical for the stability and resilience of the Earth system as a whole and formulates a safe operating space that safeguards Earth's interglacial state and resilience [M2 s6].
questions.note: Option a also paraphrases part of the slide ('ranges historically known'), but is incomplete; b and c match the slide wording.

questions.stem: Which of the following is one of the planetary boundaries that is still within the safe operating space?
questions.stemId: Manakah dibawah ini yang merupakan salah satu dari planetary boundaries yang masih dalam batasan safe operating space?
questions.explanation: In the 2025 update seven of nine boundaries are transgressed; the two still safe are stratospheric ozone depletion and atmospheric aerosol loading, while land-system change and biosphere integrity (genetic) are breached [M2 s7].
questions.note: 'Tropospheric ozone' is not one of the nine boundaries (stratospheric is).

Terperangkapnya panas akibat penebalan lapisan gas rumah kaca

questions.explanation: A thinner stratospheric ozone layer lets more of the sun's (UV) radiation reach the Earth; the other options confuse ozone with the greenhouse effect (general knowledge, slides only list the boundary) [M2 s7].

Berikut merupakan gambaran dari the great pacific garbage patch, salah satu titik penumpukan sampah terbesar di muka bumi pada perairan pasifik akibat dari pergerakan arus dan gyre. Fenomena ini terjadi akibat pelepasan sampah plastik pada wilayah DAS (daerah aliran sungai) yang akhirnya bergerak menuju daerah hilir lautan. Selain menjadi bukti nyata pelanggaran freshwater change (pada wilayah hulu), peristiwa ini juga menunjukan pelanggaran…

1) 1,2,3,4,5,....,100

Merujuk kepada pandangan malthusian mengenai pertumbuhan populasi dan pangan manakah diantara kedua ini yang merupakan pertumbuhan populasi dan sebutkan terminologi dari pertumbuhan tersebut!
questions.explanation: Malthus: population grows exponentially (geometric) while resources/food grow arithmetically (linear); series 2 doubles each step, so it is the geometric one [M3 s5].

questions.stem: In practice, Malthusian theory and views no longer hold in modern life because of food technology that keeps developing, so that available food and its production keep increasing. Moreover, food and population growth cannot be examined only unidimensionally but must also be examined in terms of the interaction of socio-economic factors, the environment and the damage that occurs, and the scarcity of the natural resources needed. This gave birth to a new school of thought called…
questions.stemId: Dalam praktiknya teori dan pandangan Malthusian tidak lagi berlaku dalam kehidupan modern akibat adanya penerapan teknologi pangan yang semakin berkembang seiring waktu sehingga jumlah pangan yang tersedia dan produksinya terus meningkat. Selain itu, pertumbuhan pangan dan populasi sendiri tidak hanya bisa ditinjau secara unidimensional melainkan juga harus ditinjau terhadap interaksi faktor sosial ekonominya, lingkungan dan kerusakan yang terjadi, serta kelangkaan yang dimiliki pada SDA yang dibutuhkan. Hal ini pun melahirkan aliran pandangan baru yang disebut sebagai…
questions.explanation: Neo-Malthusian theory recognises the interaction of social, economic and environmental factors that lead to environmental damage and resource scarcity [M3 s8].

questions.stem: The phenomenon in which the population of an observed area exceeds the carrying capacity of its environment is called…

See the model!
The figure is a model of the stages of the demographic transition, which shows the general pattern of global demographic development. Population growth in this graph is divided into 5 main stages aligned with the population growth graph. Using the analysis and concepts learned earlier, at which stage does the saturation point that signals overpopulation begin?
questions.stemId:
Perhatikan model berikut!
Berikut merupakan model tahapan transisi demografi yang menunjukan pola umum dalam perkembangan demografi global. Pertumbuhan populasi pada grafik ini dibagi menjadi 5 tahap utama yang diselaraskan dengan grafik pertumbuhan populasi. Menggunakan analisis dan konsep yang sudah dipelajari sebelumnya pada tahap manakah mulai terjadi titik kejenuhan yang menandakan overpopulasi?
questions.explanation: The total-population curve flattens at the end of stage 4 when it reaches its plateau, which the authors read as the saturation/carrying-capacity point; the slide itself only explains the transition phases (low growth, high growth, low growth) [M3 s13, s7].

questions.stem:
Consider the following factors!
1) Advances in science and technology
2) Improved health (nutrition, vaccines, sanitation)
3) Saturation point of food production
Referring to the previous question, which factors drive the population increase?
questions.stemId:
Perhatikan faktor faktor berikut!
1) Kemajuan IPTEK
2) Meningkatnya kesehatan (nutrisi, vaksin, sanitasi)
3) Titik saturasi produksi makanan
Merujuk kepada pertanyaan sebelumnya faktor apa saja yang mendorong terjadinya peningkatan populasi tersebut?
questions.explanation: Technology (agricultural innovation, Green Revolution) and improving health that lowers death rates push population up; a saturation point of food production would limit, not drive, growth [M3 s12, s13].

questions.stem: There are differences between the factors driving overpopulation in Global North countries (BBU, northern hemisphere) and Global South countries (BBS, southern hemisphere); the main counterintuitive characteristic that nevertheless actively drives population increase in BBS countries is…
questions.stemId: Terdapat perbedaan antara faktor pendorong overpopulasi di negara BBU (belahan bumi utara) dan BBS (belahan bumi selatan), karakteristik utama yang bersifat counterintuitive namun justru berperan aktif dalam mendorong peningkatan populasi di negara BBS adalah…
questions.explanation: Population growth falls as economic development reduces poverty and raises education and health; where poverty persists, birth rates stay high, so poverty keeps population growing [M3 s13].
questions.note: 'Counterintuitive' driver is not stated in the slides; key (poverty) follows from the demographic-transition notes but 'high fertility' is also defensible.

questions.stem: Ehrlich and Holdren defined that not only population affects the environment but the level of consumption also plays an active role in the environmental condition of a region. This also tends to apply to…
questions.stemId: Ehrlich dan Holdren mendefinisikan bahwa tidak hanya populasi yang berdampak pada lingkungan hidup melainkan tingkat konsumsi juga berperan aktif dalam kondisi lingkungan pada suatu wilayah. Hal ini pun cenderung berlaku pada negara negara…
questions.explanation: Ehrlich & Holdren (1974): impact depends on population, affluence (consumption) and technology; high-consumption (affluent) countries such as the Global North have large impact per capita even with small populations [M3 s16, s17, s24].

questions.stem: The concept and correlation of the level of consumption with the environment is directly proportional to the variables…
questions.stemId: Adapun konsep dan korelasi antara tingkat konsumsi terhadap lingkungan hidup berbanding lurus terhadap variabel…
questions.explanation: I = P x A x T: impact is proportional to population, affluence (measured by consumption level or per-capita income) and technology [M3 s17].
questions.note: Ambiguous: affluence is 'level of consumption OR per-capita income' on the slide, so option a (population, income, technology) is also defensible; key follows the wording 'tingkat konsumsi'.

questions.stem:
See the formula!
According to the Level of Environmental Impact formula, which index must be changed if environmental quality is to be improved compared with 10 years earlier, when the population experiences doubling time (grows 2x)?
options: Affluence undergoes decoupling and decreases by a factor of 1.5
questions.stemId:
Perhatikan rumus berikut!
Menurut rumus Level of Environmental Impact indeks apa yang harus diubah apabila kualitas lingkungan ingin ditingkatkan dari kondisi pada 10 tahun sebelumnya apabila populasi mengalami doubling time (bertumbuh 2x lipat)?
optionsId: Affluence (kemakmuran) mengalami decoupling dan berkurang 1.5x lipat
questions.explanation: With I = P x A x T and P doubled, A and/or T must fall enough that P x A x T < 1 of before: A x0.25 with T x1.25 gives 2 x 0.25 x 1.25 = 0.63 (impact falls), whereas A falling only 1.5x gives 2/1.5 = 1.33 (still worse) [M3 s17, s19].
questions.note: Wording ('technology increases 25%') is loose (T = pollutant per unit of good); c is the only option that unambiguously lowers I, option a works only if 'T grows' means 'impact per unit falls'.

questions.stem: Technology plays a role in improving environmental impact by increasing efficiency, reducing and controlling population, promoting renewable energy (EBT) and innovation. On the other hand, technological growth can also lead to increased consumption and exploitation, creating a paradox known as..
questions.stemId: Teknologi berperan dalam memperbaiki dampak terhadap lingkungan dengan meningkatkan efisiensi, mengurangi dan mengontrol populasi, mendorong EBT dan inovasi. Namun di sisi lain pertumbuhan teknologi juga bisa mengakibatkan peningkatan konsumsi serta eksploitasi menciptakan suatu paradoks yang dikenal sebagai..
questions.explanation: Technological progress makes resource use more efficient but also raises consumption: the Jevons Paradox [M3 s21, s22].

questions.stem: The impact of technology turns negative when…
options: The increase in consumption reaches the backfire stage
A rebound effect is followed by backfire at the same time

questions.stem:
Subak is the irrigation system of the Balinese community that is closely tied to customary law (Hukum Adat). It not only unites agriculture with religious ritual, Subak also ensures that every part of Balinese society receives its “right” to water. Subak is also a real manifestation of the philosophy “Tri Hita Karana”, which means maintaining harmony in the relationship with God, among humans, and with nature. The Balinese people's obedience to ancestral tradition has let Subak survive from the 8th century to the present.

In the context of ‘the commons’, Subak belongs to…
questions.stemId: Subak adalah sistem pengairan masyarakat Bali yang memiliki keterkaitan erat dengan Hukum Adat. Tidak hanya menyatukan pertanian dengan ritual keagamaan, subak memastikan seluruh unsur masyarakat Bali mendapatkan “haknya” atas air. Subak juga merupakan manifestasi nyata dari filosofi “Tri Hita Karana”, yang memiliki arti menjaga keharmonisan hubungan dengan Tuhan, antara manusia, dan dengan alam. Ketaatan masyarakat Bali pada tradisi leluhur membuat Subak bertahan dari abad ke-8 sampai masa kini. Dalam konteks ‘the commons’, Subak termasuk ke dalam…
questions.note: The slides do not classify Subak into one of these four labels. They list the irrigation system among man-made commons (M4 s12) and traditional knowledge/culture as an intellectual commons (M4 s11); Subak is presented as a collective social-cultural institution (M4 s24). 'Intellectual' is the best fit by elimination, but 'biotic' (water, paddy) is arguable.
questions.explanation: Subak is a man-made, culturally embedded commons: shared water managed through collective rules, rituals and Tri Hita Karana, i.e. a social-cultural (intellectual) institution rather than a marine or digital commons [M4 s12, s24].

questions.stem:
The Gersmehl Diagram depicts the dynamics of the nutrient cycle in 3 different biomes: taiga, tropical rainforest, and desert. In the diagram, nutrients are shown moving between forms: 1) litter (organic waste), 2) biomass (living things), and 3) soil. In the taiga, most nutrients are stored as litter because low temperatures inhibit decomposition and the transfer of nutrients to soil and biomass. In the tropical rainforest, most nutrients are stored as biomass because the consistently high temperature and rainfall speed up litter decomposition and litter is quickly absorbed by plant roots. In the desert, most nutrients are stored as soil because of the large amount of chemical and physical weathering, and the minimal plant formation caused by low rainfall.

The Gersmehl Diagram depicts one of the ecosystem services, namely…
questions.stemId: Gersmehl Diagram menggambarkan dinamika siklus nutrien pada 3 bioma berbeda: taiga, hutan hujan tropis, dan gurun. Dalam diagram tersebut, nutrien digambarkan berpindah-pindah bentuk dari 1) litter (sampah organik), 2) biomass (makhluk hidup), dan 3) soil (tanah). Di taiga, kebanyakan nutrien disimpan sebagai litter karena suhu yang rendah menghambat pembusukan dan transfer nutrien ke soil dan biomass. Di hutan hujan tropis, kebanyakan nutrien disimpan sebagai biomass karena suhu dan curah hujan yang stabil tinggi mempercepat dekomposisi litter dan litter cepat diserap oleh akar-akar tumbuhan. Di gurun, kebanyakan nutrien disimpan sebagai soil karena banyaknya pelapukan kimia maupun fisika, serta minimnya pembentukan tumbuhan yang disebabkan oleh sedikitnya curah hujan. Gersmehl Diagram menggambarkan salah satu jasa ekosistem, yaitu…
questions.note: The Gersmehl diagram itself is not in the slides; nutrient cycling is the standard MEA example of a supporting service, and the forest slide lists 'support energy flow and chemical cycling' (M4 s16).
questions.explanation: Nutrient cycling underlies all other services and is a supporting service; the forest example on the slide lists 'support energy flow and chemical cycling' [M4 s16].

questions.stem:
The Amazon rainforest is the largest rainforest in the world. The Amazon forest is indeed a habitat for millions of animal and plant species, but its role goes beyond that. One of the roles of the Amazon forest is maintaining climate stability. This is achieved through the high density and amount of vegetation in the Amazon forest. The trees of the Amazon absorb a great deal of water. Through transpiration, these trees release about 20 tons of water vapor every day. This water vapor then forms clouds and produces rainfall that not only keeps the forest itself humid but also affects global weather patterns. If the Amazon forest disappears, the Earth will lose one of its largest rain suppliers and become increasingly hot.

The role of the Amazon forest in the reading is as…
questions.stemId: Hutan Amazon adalah hutan hujan terluas di dunia. Hutan Amazon memang merupakan habitat bagi jutaan spesies hewan dan tumbuhan, tetapi peran keberadaannya lebih dari itu. Salah satu peran Hutan Amazon adalah menjaga kestabilan iklim. Hal ini terwujud melalui tingginya kepadatan dan jumlah vegetasi Hutan Amazon. Pohon-pohon di Hutan Amazon menyerap sangat banyak air. Melalui proses transpirasi, pohon-pohon tersebut mengeluarkan uap air hingga sekitar 20 ton setiap harinya. Uap air ini kemudian membentuk awan dan menghasilkan curah hujan yang tidak hanya menjaga kelembapan hutan itu sendiri, tetapi juga memengaruhi pola cuaca global. Jika Hutan Amazon habis, Bumi akan kehilangan salah satu pemasok hujan terbesarnya dan menjadi semakin panas. Peran Hutan Amazon dalam bacaan tersebut adalah sebagai…
questions.explanation: Climate regulation (rainfall, humidity, temperature stability) is a regulating service; the slide lists 'influence local and regional climate' and 'store atmospheric carbon' for forests [M4 s14, s16].
